proof_attempt_summary: The run derived the uniform index-two transition and two feasible interval calibrations for a structured rare-outcome AIPW model, then reached the D0.5 field-tier gate. The reviewer graded the delivered package subfield because the model is narrow, complete subsampling lacks an implementable approximation theorem, and no honest-length converse or efficiency result is proved. The cited CSW comparator lemma still overstates its epsilon range at zero; the paper-owned claims are supported only with that cited use restricted to positive epsilon.
tldr: A vanishing Bernoulli outcome mark changes the tail of an untrimmed AIPW score and moves its variance boundary to \(\beta=1\).  For the same untrimmed cross-fitted estimator, the paper proves two connected, uniformly valid \(95\%\) intervals over the full rare-outcome Holder class: an explicit finite-body cumulant root with stable-to-normal quantiles, and fixed-\(q\) complete self-normalized subsampling that avoids estimating \(\beta\), \(\rho\), \(V_P\), or stable quantiles.  Both calibrations cover fixed stable and ordinary Gaussian regimes, the exact infinite-variance Gaussian boundary, and every moving row \(\beta_n=1+t/\log n\), and both have the same regime-specific stochastic length order.
gap: Published untrimmed causal results are pointwise, generic Gaussian-plus-extremes approximations are oracle, and thresholded AIPW removes the stable branch. Chiang, Sasaki, and Wang's uniform subsampling theorem already includes the negative local oracle-score rows, but its stated class contains neither the exact infinite-variance \(\alpha=2\) boundary nor the positive local finite-variance family, whose standardized squares fail the required class-level uniform integrability; it also does not transfer fitted cross-fitted AIPW scores.
fill: The project proves a primitive uniform triangular law, ratio consistency of a measurable finite-body-corrected cumulant root, and uniform \(95\%\) coverage for one connected interval based on the requested untrimmed cross-fitted AIPW estimator.
